admitted.text: Randi reads as frightened by being seen without her perfected social face, even when exposure makes her feel intensely alive.
admitted.detail_quote: He could have the face. The face was very good. The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: Her desire for Vee reads as real and involuntary, there before she can turn it into a game.
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable, but a girlfriend offering her man a gift

admitted.text: At lunch she reads as gently leading Vee into confessing, steering her one small answer at a time.
admitted.detail_quote: So I let this beautiful idiot take me home. Sweet, pretty, completely in love with himself

admitted.text: Randi seems capable of real generosity toward Vee, especially when she publicly spends social standing to name her as dear.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi had just spent something on her, in front of the girls who decided what it was worth.

admitted.text: She seems jealous and shut out after Vee's night with Pace, and the anger comes out as an accusation that he is hoarding Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: You've got her all weekend, every weekend, and you're in no hurry, and I can't think why you would be.

admitted.text: Her strict control over food reads as something passed down from her mother and hard to talk about.
admitted.detail_quote: Her mother lived on egg whites and tofu, a thing she had told him with a knife in it

admitted.text: He seems truly committed to consent, insisting that Vee choose every step for herself.
admitted.detail_quote: He would ask it with her gathered back into herself, free to weigh it and choose

admitted.text: He also reads as a quiet orchestrator who sets up the conditions he wants and lets the other person think the choice was theirs.
admitted.detail_quote: What Vee can't see is that she was chosen in a game Randi and Pace started in bed.

admitted.text: For all his attention to bodies, he seems blind to what is going on inside Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: He looked for it, back through the evening from the gravel forward, and it was not there.

admitted.text: Randi leaving early seems to wound him in a way he can't put into words.
admitted.detail_quote: it left him in his own door with the cold coming in and something in his chest he had not been ready for

admitted.text: Daphne reads as the absent source of Pace’s respect for closed doors, while the cost of that lesson remains shadowed.
admitted.detail_quote: Daphne had built a door, once, and he had not respected it.

admitted.text: He seems loyal to Vee's private moments, even keeping them from Randi.
admitted.detail_quote: the true thing she had asked him to pretend she hadn't — and did not hand it over.

admitted.text: Pace reads as a maker whose love language is patient construction: meals, furniture, clothing, and carefully prepared experiences.
admitted.detail_quote: He wanted, before the night was out, to take the gloss well past itself.

admitted.text: She reads as starved for being chosen, especially by someone socially above her.
admitted.detail_quote: She had not been keeping the words. She had been keeping the feeling

admitted.text: Her shame seems to be her mother's voice, taken over as her own.
admitted.detail_quote: The shame was still running and she was burning through it, and his hand was under her, holding her up and pulling her in

admitted.text: She seems drawn to Randi in a way she won't let herself name.
admitted.detail_quote: the heat the picture put low in Vee was a heat she had no shelf for and would have died before naming at this table.

admitted.text: She seems to be outspending her means to keep up with Randi and with the dress.
admitted.detail_quote: that she did not have the next part, the paying-it-back part, that it would be sitting there next month

admitted.text: She reads as discovering her own agency in wanting.
admitted.detail_quote: she stopped being the nervous girl bracing on the platform and became someone who'd just found out she had a kind of power she'd never been issued.

admitted.text: Being seen without being judged seems to be remaking her.
admitted.detail_quote: she had spent the entire afternoon being seen at her most ashamed and had not, once, been found wanting.

admitted.text: Vee reads as touchingly naive, trusting both Pace and Randi completely without suspecting the coordination behind their appearances in her life.
admitted.detail_quote: And Vee thought, as she had been thinking lately and could not stop, that she had never once in her life had a friend like this.

admitted.text: She reads as quietly perceptive, with eyes only for Vee herself.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend,

admitted.text: She seems to notice something off in Randi that Vee doesn't.
admitted.detail_quote: He looked at her—" a tip of her chin toward Randi "—the way you'd look at somebody's great-aunt.

admitted.text: She seems hurt at being edged out by Randi, and she hides the hurt.
admitted.detail_quote: and by the time Cassie's eyes came back to Vee's, whatever had been in them was folded away.

admitted.text: She reads as a watchful authority who pressures Randi with warmth.
admitted.detail_quote: The not-standing was the move; Brooke was the chapter president and did not need to stand to stop someone in her own common room.

admitted.text: She seems steady and gently skeptical about new romance.
admitted.detail_quote: Everybody's different at the start. I said it about Danny.

admitted.text: She reads as a bright cheerleader who sees plainly what Pace's invitation means.
admitted.detail_quote: There's no meal at two, Vee. He's not asking you over to eat.

admitted.text: She seems to know and care for Pace, and that lends him credibility.
admitted.detail_quote: Christine fed me twice what I ordered and wouldn't put it on the bill.

admitted.text: The bench hidden under a tabletop: it reads as hidden purpose and the desire waiting under ordinary surfaces.
admitted.detail_quote: it would sit there in the middle of the room, full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The lock and deadbolt: they read as Randi sealing herself off.
admitted.detail_quote: she always locked it behind her, first thing, before anything else

admitted.text: The thinly sliced apple: it reads as rationed appetite and permission to want.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: The bottle cap pressed under her thumbnail: it reads as private self-punishment, a habit that comes back at Vee's lunches.
admitted.detail_quote: set the sharp inner edge of the cap under her thumbnail and pressed

admitted.text: The untouched bowl of stew: it reads as Randi refusing to be fed by Pace, and as their trouble.
admitted.detail_quote: She took the spoon. She drew it through the sauce, not down into the bowl, along the top of it, and tasted what it brought up

admitted.text: Euler's crossed mark: it reads as two separate things becoming one when brought together, which hints at the planned three.
admitted.detail_quote: Put them together, at right angles, and they turn into a single thing that's suddenly plain

admitted.text: Simpson's paradox: it reads as the hidden aggregate, the same facts telling a different story once you combine them.
admitted.detail_quote: Each year on its own, the first man is the better hitter. Put the two years together and the second man is.

admitted.text: Error-correcting codes: they read as messages that survive noise, and as truths repeated until they get through.
admitted.detail_quote: Say it more than once so the noise can't kill it.

admitted.text: The burgundy silk: it reads as being seen as she actually is rather than as she imagined herself.
admitted.detail_quote: He didn't make this for you," she said. "He made it to you.

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: it reads as a stand-in for Pace that she lives in until she reaches the real thing.
admitted.detail_quote: It was soft, and it was warm — not warm from a body, warm the way dry folded cloth is warm against wet skin

admitted.text: The traded green panties: they read as Vee offering up her shame as a gift.
admitted.detail_quote: the deep green of them particular and chosen, and the spot exactly where she'd put it.

admitted.text: the credit card with nothing under it: reads as the debt Vee is taking on in every register at once, spent on being seen
admitted.detail_quote: She knew that even while she did it — that she did not have the next part, the paying-it-back part, that it would be sitting there next month

admitted.text: the burning maple: desire arriving before acknowledged change, reading as Randi’s sudden recognition of Vee
admitted.detail_quote: a single tree burning orange in a field of things that had not yet decided to change

admitted.text: The pool: it reads as the place where Vee's body was hers before it became a problem.
admitted.detail_quote: the water was the one part of it that had never been taken.

admitted.text: The Chi Latte sign: it reads as being let in on a joke she had always stood outside.
admitted.detail_quote: Now she was walking under it with Randi holding the door

admitted.text: Will Vee find out that the meeting with Pace was staged by him and Randi?
admitted.detail_quote: He did glance at Randi then, briefly — the courtesy of a stranger acknowledging that there was another person at the table

admitted.text: What happened with Daphne, and what did it cost Pace?
admitted.detail_quote: it had cost him more than he had known, then, that anything could cost.

admitted.text: What is Pace hiding about his parents?
admitted.detail_quote: Something crossed him at parents — a small closing, there and gone, a door easing shut two rooms away.

admitted.text: Where did Pace's large scar come from?
admitted.detail_quote: She got the jeans open and shoved them down, shorts and all, and her hand stopped — a scar, large, high on the inside of his thigh.

admitted.text: What does the white-gold band Randi never removes mean to her?
admitted.detail_quote: And the band at her wrist — white gold, plain and heavy, no stone, nothing to it but the weight — that Vee had never once seen her without

admitted.text: Will Randi ever let Pace see past her face again?
admitted.detail_quote: the one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: What exactly does Randi mean by "us", and does she still want it?
admitted.detail_quote: torn out of her, and it went through him like the first swallow of something

admitted.text: Did anyone see Randi kiss Vee, and what would that mean for either of them?
admitted.detail_quote: She looked up at the dorm, the bank of windows, all those lit and unlit squares with anyone behind any of them

admitted.text: Is Cassie's "goodbye" a sign that the friendship is slipping away?
admitted.detail_quote: the whole word, flat and finished, the word for a longer parting than a Wednesday.

admitted.text: Can Vee cover the credit card debt she took on for the shoes?
admitted.detail_quote: she did not have the next part, the paying-it-back part

admitted.text: Can Pace and Randi repair what broke over Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: He did not know what he had done.
